LESSON: MAKING TECHNIQUES

Grade: PP2
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PICTURE
Topic 1.5: MAKING TECHNIQUES

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on MAKING TECHNIQUES. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we paint?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify painting materials • Organize learner to paint 3. What can we paint
2. use finger technique for using finger technique. painting • Learners to appreciate own

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MAKING TECHNIQUES
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
MAKING TECHNIQUES helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MAKING TECHNIQUES
Study MAKING TECHNIQUES like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify painting materials • Organize learner to paint 3. What can we paint

What this means
In this part you learn to identify painting materials • Organize learner to paint 3. What can we paint. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify painting materials • Organize learner to paint 3. What can we paint.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “MAKING TECHNIQUES” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify painting materials • Organize learner to paint 3. What can we paint. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use finger technique for using finger technique. painting • Learners to appreciate own

What this means
In this part you learn to use finger technique for using finger technique. painting • Learners to appreciate own. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use finger technique for using finger technique. painting • Learners to appreciate own.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to MAKING TECHNIQUES in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use finger technique for using finger technique. painting • Learners to appreciate own. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what MAKING TECHNIQUES is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “MAKING TECHNIQUES” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify painting materials • Organize learner to paint 3. What can we paint)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to MAKING TECHNIQUES in your own words. (skill: use finger technique for using finger technique. painting • Learners to appreciate own)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach MAKING TECHNIQUES to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify painting materials • Organize learner to paint 3. What can we paint.
3. Practise this skill: use finger technique for using finger technique. painting • Learners to appreciate own.
4. Make one local Kenya example of MAKING TECHNIQUES from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for MAKING TECHNIQUES: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study MAKING TECHNIQUES?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we paint?
2. What do we use to paint?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what MAKING TECHNIQUES means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify painting materials • Organize learner to paint 3. What can we paint.
5. Be able to: use finger technique for using finger technique. painting • Learners to appreciate own.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
